statement: Build a one-page, single-file website for Brew Lab, a small specialty coffee shop in Indiranagar, Bengaluru. It shows the menu with prices, opening hours and location, lets visitors pre-order a coffee for pickup via a prefilled WhatsApp message, and includes a beans and farms section and a loyalty-card explainer.
audience: Coffee drinkers in and around Indiranagar, Bengaluru, mostly on phones, who want to check the menu, hours and location and pre-order a coffee for pickup.
standards: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file; CDN libraries allowed; no build step.
Warm and modern look; works well on a phone.
No invented facts: unconfirmed prices, hours, address, WhatsApp number and sourcing are visibly marked placeholders or kept generic.
Total spend stays within the 100 budget; about 80 for the baseline build, about 20 held for two fixes.
rules: Pre-order opens a prefilled WhatsApp message to the shop; the site stores and sends nothing itself; payment is at pickup.
The page must say an order is confirmed only when the shop replies.
The WhatsApp number is a labeled placeholder.
Prices, opening hours and address are visibly labeled placeholders.
Beans and farms content stays generic: no invented farm names, origins or claims.
No Kannada or other extra languages unless later added by a new decision.
done_when: The site is one HTML file with CSS and JavaScript inline or loaded from CDNs, and it needs no build step.
The file has separate sections for menu, opening hours, location, beans and farms, loyalty card, and pre-order.
The menu lists several items, each with a price, and every price is visibly labeled as a placeholder.
The opening hours and the address (naming Indiranagar, Bengaluru) are present and visibly labeled as placeholders.
The loyalty section states the rule: buy 9, get the 10th free.
The pre-order form lets a visitor pick items and quantities and enter a name; its script builds the order text and opens a WhatsApp link (wa.me or api.whatsapp.com) with that text prefilled.
The WhatsApp number in the link is a labeled placeholder, defined in one clearly marked place in the file.
Near the pre-order form, the page says payment is at pickup and that the order is confirmed only when the shop replies.
The beans and farms section uses generic wording and contains no named farm, region or sourcing claim.
The file has a viewport meta tag and responsive CSS (media queries or fluid layout) so content fits a phone-width screen without sideways scrolling.
The CSS defines a warm color palette (coffee, cream or earth tones) and a modern font stack.
All visible text is in English.
A visible list or note on the page shows which details are still placeholders.
open_inputs: Real street address and map location
Real bean details, farm names and sourcing facts
Whether Kannada or any other language is wanted later
